claim: NullPropagatedOperands recurses into Left and Right of every SqlBinaryExpression regardless of OperatorType, so AndAlso/OrElse operands are registered as null-propagating; under three-valued logic NULL AND FALSE = FALSE and NULL OR TRUE = TRUE, so DropNotNullChecks deletes the IS NOT NULL guard and the query returns true/false where it must return null. The same file already carries the carve-out at :2314-2321.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: `NullPropagatedOperands` treats `AndAlso`/`OrElse` as null-propagating, so the `IS NOT NULL` guard is deleted from a CASE whose result is a boolean `AND`/`OR` — query returns `true`/`false` where it must return `null`

claim: On SQL Server a boolean is a search condition, not a value; SearchConditionConvertingExpressionVisitor runs after nullability processing and lifts the bare condition with a two-arm CASE WHEN cond THEN 1 ELSE 0 END that has no NULL arm, so stripping the CASE ... ELSE NULL END loses the NULL even for genuinely null-propagating operators (e.g. x.NullableIntA != null ? (bool?)(x.NullableIntA > x.IntB) : null yields false instead of null).
raw: #2 🔴 Critical: Dropping the guard on a **boolean-typed** result loses the `NULL` on SQL Server even for genuinely null-propagating operators — `SearchConditionConvertingExpressionVisitor` re-wraps the bare condition with `ELSE CAST(0 AS bit)`

claim: The five new tests use only bitwise ~, integer + and string concatenation as the CASE result — all genuinely null-propagating, non-boolean operators — so all pass; no added test puts &&, || or a comparison operator into clause.Result, the exact class the optimization miscompiles. The fixture data would have caught both regressions.
